study_identification.title: Age-atypical brain functional networks in autism spectrum disorder: a normative modeling approach

study_characteristics.study_objective: Using ABIDE resting-state fMRI, build age-dependent normative models of network functional connectivity to quantify individual deviations (W-scores) in ASD and test associations with behavioral symptoms.

dataset_name.reason: Participants were sourced entirely from ABIDE; explicitly stated in Participants and Supplement 1.
dataset_name.supporting_text: All the data analyzed in this study were sourced from the ABIDE dataset.

hc_sex.supporting_text: it also has few female participants, with a male-to-female ratio of approximately 5:1.

deviation_metric.answer: W-score (network-wise deviation from TD norm); Z' score (edge-wise); outlier threshold |deviation| > 2 SD; extreme value distribution for maximum deviation summary

These statistical norms were then used to compute the Z'-scores ... hypothesis testing on the W-scores after removing subject outliers ... truncation at ±2 S.D. ... averaging the trimmed 1% highest absolute deviations ... fitting an extreme value distribution ...

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Spearman correlations between network W-scores and SRS subscale scores with FDR correction (pcorrected<0.05). Significant negative correlations observed especially in DMN, FPN, and OCN (e.g., DMN with SRS_awareness r=-0.192, p=0.028; FPN with SRS_cognition r=-0.262, p=0.001; OCN with SRS_cognition r=-0.243, p=0.002).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: ASD shows age-atypical, individualized network FC trajectories; outlier rates increase with age in ASD and decrease with age in TD; deviations associate with ASD symptom severity, notably in DMN.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Network-wise normative modeling identified individuals with |deviation|>2 SD. Outlier rates in TD decreased with age, whereas ASD increased. Significant negative associations between W-scores and SRS subscales were strongest in DMN, FPN, and OCN: DMN within-network FC vs SRS_awareness r=-0.192 (pcorr=0.028), SRS_cognition r=-0.101 (pcorr=0.025), SRS_mannerisms r=-0.153 (pcorr=0.045); FPN within-network FC vs SRS_cognition r=-0.262 (pcorr=0.001), SRS_communication r=-0.112 (pcorr=0.021), SRS_mannerisms r=-0.183 (pcorr=0.007); OCN within-network FC vs SRS_cognition r=-0.243 (pcorr=0.002), SRS_communication r=-0.145 (pcorr=0.013), SRS_mannerisms r=-0.176 (pcorr=0.008).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Cross-sectional only; ComBat may remove meaningful variance—HBR suggested as preferable; W-scores based on two means may lose precision; limited age coverage (<early childhood, late adulthood) and few females (~5:1 M:F); LOESS-based SD estimates may be unstable in sparse age bins (excluded bins with ≤2 subjects); motion remains a key confound.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Six-network Dosenbach160 parcellation; 23 network-level W-scores; LOESS age modeling with R optim bandwidth selection; ComBat harmonization with diagnosis as biological variable; bootstrapping/permutation reliability; extreme value statistics to summarize maximum deviation.

general_notes.general_notes: Age groups for some analyses: 5-11, 12-17, 18-30. Left-handed participants excluded. MPRAGE available in ABIDE but not used. Network labels: DMN, FPN, CON, SMN, OCN, CEN.
